subject: URGENT: Post-demo capacity incident - Hosted -> Dedicated qualification
messages:
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Singh <bob.singh@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: Hosted capacity incident / next steps

Hi Rishi -

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. During our POC run at ~11:32 UTC we saw severe throttling from the Hosted API which caused a downstream web job to fail and triggered an incident for our ops team. We're attaching a terse incident scrub (incident_scrub.pdf) with timestamps.

High level: we were sending parallel requests at ~120 concurrent requests (avg request ~400 tokens, worst-case burst ~900 tokens) and saw elevated 5xx/429s for ~3 minutes. For context, this is a customer-facing flow so 3 minute outages are not acceptable.

Two asks:
- Can you confirm whether this is an expected throttling behavior for Hosted at our usage profile?
- What are the options to avoid this for production - Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC - and roughly how fast can we get a migration path?

We want to decide quickly; if Dedicated can be provisioned fast we may move that direction.

Thanks,
Alice Jensen
Senior Engineering Manager | ACME Corp
alice.jensen@acme.com

Attachment: incident_scrub.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted capacity incident / next steps

Hi Alice - thanks for the quick note and the scrub. I'm sorry you hit that during the POC - I understand how disruptive that is.

Short answers up front: Hosted can support sustained traffic but at your peak burst/parallelism we expect higher latency and throttling unless we configure dedicated capacity or apply conservative rate limiting. From the details you sent it sounds like you exceeded the default concurrency/throughput profile for your account.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick 30-minute call today to triage the scrub and confirm exact QPS/tokens patterns (I'll set up if you're available).
2) Dev will analyze the metrics snapshot and recommend whether Dedicated or Private is appropriate. Typically Dedicated capacity removes the shared throttles and gives predictable throughput; Private is a longer-term option for network isolation and compliance (VPC/HSM).
3) Commercial: Marissa can outline options for a fast Dedicated trial and temporary burst capacity while we onboard you.

Can you share a raw sample of requests/min and your SLOs (p95 latency target, acceptable error budget)? If you prefer, we can start provisioning a small Dedicated pool as an expedited mitigation while we evaluate.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 17:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted capacity incident / next steps

On Wed, 25 Mar 2026 at 16:05, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Short answers up front: Hosted can support sustained traffic but at your peak burst/parallelism we expect higher latency and throttling unless we configure dedicated capacity or apply conservative rate limiting.

Thanks for the context - I pulled the account-side metrics and attached a snapshot (hosted_metrics_snapshot.png). From what I can see: the burst at 11:32 aligned with a spike in concurrent KV-cache misses and the autoscaler's backoff period. Hosted is designed for multi-tenant isolation and will surface throttles when a single customer exceeds the target concurrency for the shared pool.

Two recommended technical mitigations:
- Short term (hours): we can apply a per-account concurrency increase and temporary burst credits to reduce 429s while we run a deeper analysis. This is a stopgap and not ideal if you require strict SLOs.
- Medium term (48-72 hours with priority): provision a Dedicated pool with pinned GPUs and throughput SLOs. This removes the shared throttles and gives predictable p95 latency.

To size the Dedicated pool we need:
- sustained RPS (requests/sec) and peak concurrent requests
- average and p95 token lengths per request
- target p95 latency (eg 300ms / 500ms)

I can scope a 48hr expedited provisioning if you confirm numbers.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: hosted_metrics_snapshot.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Hosted capacity incident / next steps

Hi Alice - looping in commercial next steps. We can absolutely move quickly:

Option A - Dedicated (recommended given incident):
- Lead time: 48-72 hours for a priority provision (we can frontload provisioning while we finalize paperwork).
- Workload commit: we'll ask for a 1-3 month trial commit to cover the expedited capacity; we can set a short-term retainer and reconcile on month 1 usage.
- Pricing: I can share a one-page addendum and get DocuSign ready; if leadership approves we can provision on signature.

Option B - Temporary Hosted fixes:
- Apply temporary burst credits and raise concurrency limits for 12-48 hours while we onboard Dedicated. This is a bridge, not a permanent fix.

Security/compliance: if you'd like Private (VPC/HSM), that's a longer intake (weeks) and typically required for enterprise regulatory needs.

I'll open a DocuSign addendum and escalate to our provisioning team. For the trial we typically need a short MOU + billing contact. I'll attach the DocuSign link once created.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Thanks all - we want to move forward with a Dedicated trial ASAP.

Requested sizing (for provisioning):
- Sustained RPS: 30 req/s
- Peak concurrent requests: 140
- Avg tokens/request: 420; p95 tokens: 880
- Target p95 latency: <= 500ms

We also need a quick security/Q&A: our security team will share a short SOC2 checklist (attached: SOC2-request.xlsx). Can you confirm:
- Estimated time to provision Dedicated (assuming paperwork signed today)
- Will provisioning include KV cache warming options or do we need a warm-up traffic plan?
- Who is the technical point of contact for onboarding?

If you can provision within 48-72 hours we'll accept the expedited trial. We'll sign the addendum today if you send the DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Alice Jensen
